data.title: Default or Weak Service Credentials
data.summary: Services were reachable with vendor default or trivially guessable credentials, granting administrative access without any exploitation. This is consistently the fastest route from network access to control of a device or application.
data.description:
Default credentials survive because the device works without changing them. Management interfaces, printers and MFPs, hypervisors, out-of-band controllers such as iDRAC and iLO, network appliances, database instances, CI runners and monitoring dashboards are all commonly deployed and then left as shipped.

An attacker needs no vulnerability: the credentials are published in the vendor's own documentation and collected in public lists. The resulting access is usually administrative, and the device often sits outside the patching and monitoring applied to servers.

Out-of-band management deserves separate mention, because access there is equivalent to physical access — remote console, virtual media, and power control, below the operating system and beneath most monitoring.
data.recommendation:
* Change every default credential as part of commissioning, before the device is reachable from a production network.
* Inventory devices with management interfaces, including printers, cameras, and out-of-band controllers.
* Place management interfaces on a dedicated, access-controlled network, never routable from user subnets.
* Scan the estate periodically for known default credentials rather than relying on the build process.
data.short_recommendation: Change every default credential before a service is reachable.
